summary: Our team built an interactive web-browser app that serves as a fun game for kids to learn survival skills on a Martian outpost by balancing needs like life support, radiation shielding, power and food production. You play as a botanist on Juniper Base who is stranded until the rescue ship (Kestrel) lands. You play through events like dust storms and solar waves which impact the decisions you make in the game. Our team used the DONKI (API) solar-flare records and OSDR crop-study records to influence things such as growth time and in-game hazards. The data being used is adapted for play. Our game moves learners from just reading facts to actually surviving and explaining their own decisions. It’s designed for kids aged 7 - 12 to immerse themselves as an actual astronaut in space, and learn to experiment with the variables provided while still having a blast.
details: Red Planet Garden is an interactive game that takes place on Mars and teaches kids about the challenges of sustaining human life on another planet where circumstances are different. They manage a Martian base by balancing resources such as air, water, food, and power. They can grow crops in a greenhouse as well as upgrade equipment to respond to potential challenges such as dust storms and solar flares. Our game benefits the kids playing because it incorporates real NASA scientific research (DONKI space weather data and the Open Science Data Repository) into an interactive game environment for kids to learn. The game is primarily run on JavaScript. The simulation, Sprouts logic, saving and NASA data calls. The rest is small (HTML for the on screen panels. CSS for how the panels and buttons look. GLSL for a few lines of shader code, the Mars sky, and the solar glow. SVG for the drawn icons). Our game creatively combines survival gameplay with real world space discoveries and data. instead of teaching players about Mars, our game allows kids to experience challenges of what living there would be like through interactive farming and management of resources. Our team considered scientific accuracy, gameplay enjoyment and educational as we aimed to give our players the most fun way of understanding what life on Mars would look like.
